title: Kickstart: 30-minute integration angles for engineers
content:
Context:
This is a working brief for the Hosted API go-to-market micro-experiments aimed specifically at software engineers and engineering managers. The goal: reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) to under 30 minutes and provide crystal-clear pricing language that maps to developer risk tolerances.

Audience & user jobs:
- Individual engineers evaluating an LLM API: wants minimal setup, predictable latency, a clear example that returns useful output quickly.
- Engineering leads deciding on an API for product integration: cares about cost predictability, SLAs, and escape hatches (rollback/pinning).
- Platform/infra teams validating procurement risk: want deterministic billing, data handling assurances, and SDKs that fit existing stacks.

Developer-first value props (short lines for copy and hero variants):
- "Get a working LLM demo in 30 minutes — real tokens, real latency, no vendor lock-in."
- "Same API surface across hosted, dedicated, and private — ship once, run anywhere."
- "Transparent perf profiles: choose latency or cost-optimized variants with one flag."
- "Predictable per-token pricing + free starter credits to validate in production-like workloads."

Quickstart angles (recipes + what to measure):
1) "30-min chat widget" (target: frontend engineer)
   - Steps: 1) npm install redwood-inference; 2) wire API key; 3) copy paste 10-line chat handler; 4) run sample UI with streaming.
   - Outcome: streaming response visible in UI, first token latency < 200ms in hosted region.
   - Metrics: TTFS, first-token-latency, tokens generated in trial.

2) "Serverless snippet + cost baseline" (target: backend dev)
   - Steps: 1) deploy 50-line serverless function using sample prompt; 2) run load script at 10 rps for 1 minute; 3) inspect token and latency breakdown in Console.
   - Outcome: baseline cost per 1k tokens and 95th percentile latency.
   - Metrics: cost-per-1k, p95 latency, error rate.

3) "Embeddings for search in <1 hour" (target: search/product dev)
   - Steps: 1) run embeddings script on 100 docs; 2) insert vectors into open-source vector DB; 3) run similarity queries.
   - Outcome: semantic search returning relevant results; embed unit costs and batch sizing recommendations surfaced.

Onboarding microcopy and subject lines (for emails/in-app):
- Subject: "Your Redwood API key is ready — try a live demo in 30 minutes"
- CTA: "Run the 30-min starter"
- Microcopy for console: "Start with the example that matches your stack. Tokens are metered — your free credits cover ~X API calls."

Pricing language drafts (experiment variants):
Variant A — developer-friendly and direct:
  "Pay per token you use. Free starter credits for developers to validate real requests. View precise cost and latency per route in the Console so you can pick the right model for production."

Variant B — risk-focused, emphasizes predictability:
  "Simple per-token pricing plus burstable free credits. When you’re ready to commit, Reserved Capacity gives you a predictable monthly rate and priority throughput — ideal for production workloads."

Variant C — comparison-friendly (for platform buyers):
  "Transparent per-token rates; detailed perf profiles available. Avoid hidden ops costs — we surface batching and caching recommendations that lower your per-token bill by X–Y% compared to out-of-the-box usage."

Pricing microcopy experiments (for pricing page & sign-up flow):
- "Estimated monthly cost calculator" — show a live calc using sample traffic (messages/day, average tokens).
- On free tier: "Starter credits are intended for evaluation and small pilots. If you exceed them, you’ll be prompted to add billing and see a projected cost before any charge."

Competitive positioning notes (quick bullets for sales/comm):
- Comp set: hyperscale cloud AI endpoints, single-model API providers, self-hosted inference platforms.
- Differentiators to highlight: production-grade serving (latency SLOs), consistent API across deployment modes, per-route perf and cost transparency, and SDK ergonomics for modern stacks.
- Weaknesses to pre-empt: "We aren’t the cheapest per-token on every workload — we win on predictable latency, rollout controls, and operational transparency."

Risky claims to avoid:
- Avoid absolute cost savings percentages without context (workload, sequence length).
- Don’t promise "zero ops" for Private deployments — emphasize support and automation instead.

A/B test ideas (ranked by expected signal):
- Pricing copy: Variant A vs Variant B on sign-up conversion and trial-to-paid conversion.
- Quickstart length: 30-minute vs 90-minute walkthroughs impact TTFS and retention for devs.
- CTA phrasing: "Start a live demo" vs "Run sample code" — measure clicks and activation.

Ops & success metrics for the campaign:
- Short term (30d): TTFS median, trial activation rate (API calls made), % of trials that create a production credential.
- Mid term (90d): conversion to paid, % that upgrade to Reserved Capacity, retention by developer cohort.
- Qualitative: feedback notes in in-app survey: "Was the quickstart helpful?" (1–5) and top-suggested missing pieces.

Handy snippets for docs & UI (copy-ready):
- "30-min starter: from signup to first streaming response."
- "Turn on metrics in Console to see per-route cost and latency breakdowns."
- "Pin model versions to avoid surprises during rollout."

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Decide default example stacks to support: React + Next, FastAPI, Node Express, Python Flask.
- What is the free starter credits equivalency (tokens / $) for copy? Need product to finalize.
- Should we add a short video demo (90s) to the signup flow? Recommendation: yes, test in cohort.

Pull requests & next steps:
- Product: confirm the free credits amount and exact per-token tiers. (Jin to follow up with pricing team).
- DX: finalize the 30-min starter repo, add one-click deploy for Vercel and Cloud Run. (Maya)
- Growth: build two landing page variants wired to experiment flags (A/B pricing copy + CTA). (Sofia)

Notes to self: keep the language concise and engineer-focused; show code early; surface performance and cost numbers quickly so peers can evaluate trade-offs.
summary: Working brief: 30-min developer quickstarts, messaging variants, and pricing-language experiments for Hosted API. Focus: TTFS, transparency, measurable A/B tests.
